title: An AI Dark Horse Is Rewriting the Rules of Game Design
author: wiredmagazine

comments.author: wiredmagazine
comments.body:
The video game [Valorant](https://playvalorant.com/en-us/), a fast-paced [team-based shooter](https://www.wired.com/story/riot-games-valorant-impressions/), has recently become a testing ground for a promising new direction in [artificial intelligence](https://www.wired.com/tag/artificial-intelligence/) research. The game’s developers at Riot Games (a Tencent subsidiary) are using 3D-native AI models to prototype new characters, scenes, and storylines, according to a researcher familiar with the company’s efforts who spoke on the condition of anonymity.

While many AI models can generate text, images, and video, Tencent’s [Hunyuan](https://hunyuan.tencent.com/) (混元 or “first mix”) family of models can dream up 3D objects and interactive scenes. The source says that Tencent’s models are also being used by the developers of another Tencent game, [GKART](https://www.wtfast.com/en/games/gkart/?srsltid=AfmBOopXOKUQ5TRGh3p2ph_lFusjM1z2vxJcIPyeHK9P6M200kJkRZkY), and by some independent developers, too. Tencent declined to comment.

“The games industry requires a lot of investment,” the source says. “Previously you would need a month to design a character. Now you can just type in some text, and Hunyuan can give you four choices in 60 seconds.”

The news is an early signal that models capable of understanding and re-creating the physical world could become a standard ingredient in game design. In addition to generating game content, these models could also enable more advanced virtual and augmented reality and help robots learn to do new things.

“There’s a real explosion of 3D vision research nowadays,” says [Alexander Raistrick](https://araistrick.github.io/), a graduate student at Princeton University working on novel approaches to generating 3D content. “There are many killer applications: There's content creation, there’s self driving, and there’s a whole stack of problems involved in augmented reality.”

Raistrick adds that video games are an obvious application for 3D AI models. “Outputting 3D meshes \[a standard way of representing 3D objects\] is your typical kind of bread and butter of game development,” he says.

But, as in other creative fields, using AI to create video games is controversial. Concerns about AI-fueled [job loss loom large](https://www.wired.com/story/ai-is-already-taking-jobs-in-the-video-game-industry/). Some developers say [games should be labeled](https://www.gamesradar.com/games/valve-artist-says-thats-like-saying-food-products-shouldnt-have-their-ingredients-list-as-epics-tim-sweeney-and-more-call-on-steam-to-drop-the-made-with-ai-label/) when they contain AI-made content. Others say it’s too late: The technology is already ubiquitous in the industry.

Read the full story here: [https://www.wired.com/story/tecent-3d-models-video-game-design-artificial-intelligence/](https://www.wired.com/story/tecent-3d-models-video-game-design-artificial-intelligence/)

replies.author: JustSomeCarioca
replies.body: It's worth mentioning that unlike most others that offer similar services, it is free.

replies.author: fungnoth
replies.body: If I were tencent, I wouldn't do it with an existing brand. I would make another new name for it, the west would over react to any AI related stuff

replies.author: JustSomeCarioca
replies.body: What do you mean another name? They've been using Hunyuan for all of their releases. From video to imagery to sound and 3D. They've been very consistent about it. But there's no reason for the West to overreact because it's not like they're the only players out there. They're the only ones that are free that's all. But a quick search will turn up a bunch of rivals that are exceptionally competent and certainly not inferior. And most people just react emotionally to the idea that it's Chinese. It's no different than the complete and absolute domination of Open Source LLMs by the Chinese now.

comments.author: Mammoth-Minimum-5588
comments.body: Is this about 3D art design or the actual game design?

replies.author: FjorgVanDerPlorg
replies.body:
3d Art for these in-house models right now. So they use text prompt and have a 3d model, potentially skipping a lot of concept/design steps in the process. From there I assume a 3d artist would unfuck all the mistakes, eg a lot of models do word salad shaped "text" etc.

This one won't be public facing, but it means AI augmented art is coming to games now.

Ironically the very AI goldrush for compute this is fueling is gonna hurt tencent and the rest of the gaming market in the near future, because who the fuck can afford GPUs or RAM right now, 64gb for $640 USD (trending towards $900) is wild and that's if you can even get it. There is gonna be a extended tech stagnation in gaming and when parts break, the chances they don't get replaced are now much higher. This is gonna hurt their bottom line and starting soon too. Not just PC, it's consoles as well and the rest of computer gaming
